subject: Post-demo: model-fit options, eval pack, and safety guardrails
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Turner <alicia@quantumretail.com>
Cc: David Kline <david.kline@quantumretail.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: model-fit options, eval pack, and safety guardrails

Hi Alicia (and David),

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the clear context on your high-throughput SKU normalization use case and examples. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our call:
- Goal: extract and normalize SKU attributes (brand, size, variant) from merchant product descriptions with high precision and low hallucination on unseen SKUs.
- Volume: ~1.2M inference calls/month with 99th percentile latency target under 350ms for production traffic.
- Risk: downstream inventory automation requires near-zero SKU hallucination; tolerance for spurious new SKUs is very low.

Immediate recommendations (what we'll deliver this week):
1) Eval pack: I attached a starter prompt set (eval_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short harness we recommend for your dataset. This includes batch prompts and labels format.
2) Candidate models: propose we validate rw-7b-v2 (fast) and rw-13b-quant (higher quality on rare tokens). We'll run both on a 5k sample you approve.
3) Safety guardrails: add explicit hallucination checks (exact-match SKU verification, confidence thresholds, and a fallback to deterministic rules for low-confidence outputs).
4) Version safety: if you see quality regressions after model updates we can pin to a specific model build for your account while we run diffs. See runbook link I'll share in the follow-up.

Next steps:
- Alicia: share a 5k sample subset (anonymized) or give us access to the sample folder.
- Redwood: we will run the two candidate models, return a short benchmark (precision/recall/exact-match/hallucination-rate + latency P50/P95), and recommend pin/rollforward options.
- Tentative timeline: bench results in 48 business hours after we receive sample.

I'll loop in Monica (solutions) and Rishi (solutions lead for retail) to scope the eval and a short safety mitigation plan.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0129

Hi Michael — thanks for the recap, this is helpful. We can share the 5k sample today; I uploaded a folder with 5k anonymized items to the link below (read-only).

Quick note and a small escalation:
- Yesterday our engineering team noticed a spike in bad normalizations after a vendor pushed a model variant in our proof-of-concept environment. Specifically, several SKUs that previously returned deterministic canonical ids now produced hallucinated sku_codes (non-existent). That triggered a few failed automations and a rollback.
- We need to know: what are our options to immediately stop the new variant from being used in production (pining/rollback), and how fast can Redwood isolate us on the previous model build? We're still in trial but this is blocking a mid-Feb procurement check.

I've added David (procurement) on cc — he's looking for a short note on operational controls (pin timing, rollback SLA, and whether pinning is reversible without data loss).

Link to sample: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QTR-QuantumRetail-eval-pack

If you can provide the bench results + a short runbook for emergency pin/rollback we'd appreciate it. Also confirm you received the sample.

Best,
Alicia Turner
Head of Product Operations | QuantumRetail

Folks — forwarding the call recap and the escalation from Alicia. Key asks from the customer:
- Run targeted regression diffs between their current production model build and the earlier build they were using (they saw hallucinated SKUs after a vendor push).
- Provide a short, traffic-safe pinning plan: whether we can pin them to the prior model build for the account and for how long (customer prefers immediate pin while we complete the eval).
- Deliver the bench (precision/recall/EM/hallucination-rate + latency P50/P95) on the 5k sample.

Please treat as priority — procurement is looking for a one-pager. If pinning is a quick config we should do a temporary pin (24-72h) to restore trust and buy time for the eval.

Alicia, David: Monica and Rishi will own the technical triage and come back with an ETA.

Thanks,
Michael

Subject: RE: Fwd: QuantumRetail sample + regression flag — please triage

Thanks for the nudge, Michael — looping in plan and immediate actions.

Short answer on pin/rollback: yes, we can pin an account to a specific model build or rollback to a previous "release" variant. For hosted customers like QuantumRetail we support per-account model pins; changes are config-only and reversible. Timeline: we can apply an account-level pin within 1 business hour once we have the target model id. The pin can be applied for any duration and removed after verification.

Proposed triage + mitigation plan (48h fast path):
1) Immediate mitigation (1 hour): temporary pin to the last known-good build (we need confirmation of the build id from your side; if you don't have it we can identify the last build that matched your golden sample). This prevents further bad calls in prod.
2) 24-48h investigation: run regression diffs across the 5k sample. Metrics:
   - Exact-match rate (EM) on canonical SKU ids
   - Hallucination rate (outputs that map to non-existent SKU ids)
   - Confidence distribution and low-confidence fallback rate
   - Latency P50/P95
3) Remediation options: re-tune prompt templates, add deterministic post-checks, or recommend switching to rw-13b-quant for the poorest-performing buckets.

Candidate models to validate:
- rw-7b-v2: lower latency, good baseline.
- rw-13b-quant: better handling of rare tokens and proper names, lower hallucination on sparse SKUs.
- If you need the absolute lowest hallucination, we can also test the rw-13b-20270114 build (previous stable build for many retail customers).

Deliverables we'll provide:
- Bench report (CSV + short slide): precision/recall/EM/hallucination + latency summary.
- Diff log: sample inputs with side-by-side outputs across builds and a short commentary.
- Pin runbook snippet: exactly how we apply/remove pins and audit logs (link).

Attachments: quantum_eval_instructions.pdf (contains harness commands and expected outputs).

Requested from you:
- Confirm whether you want us to apply an immediate temporary pin to rw-13b-20270114 or if you prefer we first identify the last-good build.
- Share any pass/fail rules you currently use for SKU normalization (we'll incorporate them in the bench).

If you confirm pin now we will: apply account pin, run the 5k bench overnight, and send the diff report with recommendations tomorrow EOD PST.

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
